title: Core Web Vitals Explained: LCP, INP & CLS
description:
👉 Frontend System Design Essentials — Course: https://icodeit.thinkific.com/courses/frontend-system-design-essentials

👉 Frontend System Design Essentials — Book: https://leanpub.com/frontend-system-design-essentials/

Intro

“Is it fast?” depends on device, network, and what you measure. Core Web Vitals give teams a small, user-aligned set of signals: LCP for when the main on-screen content finishes rendering, INP for how snappy interactions feel (not just the first tap), and CLS for whether the layout jumps and breaks trust. This episode explains each vital in plain terms, what kinds of frontend decisions they push on (critical path, main-thread work, reserved space for media), why lab and field data both matter, and how optimizing one vital can trade off against another—so you treat them as explicit design constraints, not a single score to game.

You'll Learn

- Why classic timings like load or TTFB don’t fully capture perceived quality
- What LCP measures, what typically hurts it, and how it ties to critical rendering and above-the-fold content
- What INP adds beyond first-input metrics and why it reflects main-thread contention and long tasks
- What CLS penalizes and how to think about dimensions, fonts, and late-injected UI
- How the three vitals map to different architectural pressures and common trade-offs between them
- How lab vs field measurement fits into iteration versus real-user ground truth

Final Takeaway

Core Web Vitals aren’t the only performance metrics that matter, but they’re a durable shared language for user-perceived loading, interactivity, and stability. Treating LCP, INP, and CLS as three constraints—delivery, runtime, and layout composition—helps you negotiate trade-offs in large frontends instead of chasing one misleading “fast” number.
